title: Flip String to Monotone Increasing
summary: Given a binary string, determine the least number of flips needed to transform it into a sequence where all zeros precede all ones.
statement: Given a binary string, determine the least number of flips needed to transform it into a sequence where all zeros precede all ones.
constraints: Flip individual bits so the result is nondecreasing: some zeros followed by some ones.
hints: At each position track ones seen and best flips for a monotone prefix.
A zero is either flipped, or all previous ones are flipped.
For zero set flips=min(flips+1,ones); for one increment ones.
These are the only ways a monotone prefix can end after a zero.
editorial: These are the only ways a monotone prefix can end after a zero.

tests.explanation: Flipping the final zero gives 00111 with one change.
Two flips are sufficient, for example producing 011111.
